definition: Explicit integration of qualitative and quantitative components
Interviews, focus groups, ethnography, qualitative document or media analysis, whether at one time point or several
Single-subject or case-study designs
Simulation, in silico, pharmacometric or systems models whose output is the main result
Chemical synthesis, structural or analytical characterization of compounds or materials, with no experimental comparison
Conditions assigned at random by the investigator: RCTs, randomized laboratory or vignette experiments
Investigator manipulates exposure or treatment with a comparison, randomization not stated: most animal, in vitro and dose–response work

Treatment not assigned by the investigator, analyzed with a comparison built for causal inference: natural experiments, difference-in-differences, interrupted time series, regression discontinuity, synthetic control
One group measured before and after an intervention, no comparison
Repeated measures on the same units, no manipulation
One time point, associational or descriptive
Two or more designs, none carrying the main qualifying aim
How much, where, in whom, over time: prevalence, incidence, trends, disparities
Why use, misuse or addiction occurs: risk and protective factors, etiology, processes producing addiction phenomena. Substance use is the **outcome**
What substance use or exposure does: physiological, organ, developmental, cognitive, psychiatric, behavioral, social, academic, occupational or justice outcomes. Substance use is the **exposure**
How a substance or compound acts: binding, selectivity, potency, pharmacokinetics, structure–activity, characterized toward understanding or development
Developing or testing an intervention to prevent, detect, treat, or support recovery from substance use/SUD or explicitly substance-related harms and conditions
How care or programs are organized, delivered, staffed, financed, accessed, adopted or scaled, including organizational policy
Laws, regulation, enforcement, markets, prices or economic conditions as causes or objects
Stigma, discourse, identity, norms, or public and professional attitudes as the principal object or outcome
Training, curricula, competencies or professional preparation as the object
Developing or evaluating a measure, assay, method, platform or paradigm where its performance is primary
The objective is clear but no listed category fits; review each use
Different qualifying objectives carry the aims equally
Molecules, receptors, compounds, cells, tissue, or biospecimens studied as material
Whole living non-human organisms
Individual people, including their brains, physiology and behavior
Couples, parent–child dyads, families, peer or therapy groups as units
Clinics, treatment programs, schools, agencies, workplaces, provider organizations
Neighborhoods, counties, states, countries, or population aggregates
Documents, media, policies or online content as units
Two or more levels carry the conclusions equally
Self-report instruments, questionnaires, rating scales, vignette responses, whether author-administered or from an existing survey
Interviews, focus groups, field notes, observation, open-ended text from participants
Laboratory tasks, cognitive or neuropsychological tests, observed or recorded behavior, self-administration
Biospecimens, biomarkers, physiology, toxicology, clinical measurements
MRI, PET, EEG, electrophysiology, other brain measures
Genotypes, sequencing, gene expression, epigenetics
Compound synthesis, binding and functional assays, analytical or forensic chemistry
Electronic health records, claims, prescription or treatment records, registries, vital statistics, poison-center reports
Justice, education, social service or program operations records
Policies, laws, media, social media, websites, published literature
Geographic, outlet-density, price, market or environmental data
Data generated by simulation or models
